Google shows Argon helping Apollo learn cornhole through simulation

Seven consecutive successful throws follow practice and physical feedback, rather than demonstrating a first-attempt success rate.

Humanoids Daily ↗13 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 3

From observation to simulation

Google showed Gemini 4 Argon observing a human cornhole video, helping construct a MuJoCo environment and refining movement before transfer to Apptronik’s Apollo. The company demonstrated seven consecutive successful throws.

Physical feedback is part of the process

The account includes stance, swing and release adjustments using bag landing positions on real hardware. The streak supplies neither the total attempt count nor the human engineering effort, so it cannot establish general accuracy or first-attempt success.

Keep generated plans separate

Another linked demonstration uses Argon to iteratively steer Gemini Omni video toward spelling ARGON; it is a generated plan, not evidence of that physical task. The reported 87% ERQA score is an image-and-text reasoning result, not an 87% robot task-success rate.
